kit.purpose: Pre-launch ready-to-drink coffee for India. The name is a session alias and is not a brand already on shelf.

marketPack.household: Joint and nuclear households both appear. A can is often bought for one person and noticed by the rest of the house.
marketPack.paymentRails: UPI and cash. Kirana still matters beside Blinkit and Amazon.
taboos: Do not call the drink a health or protein product.
Do not default to US latte language.

cohorts.label: Office sipper
cohorts.rule: Office sippers 25–34 · metros · bought RTD coffee 90d

cohorts.label: Value household
cohorts.rule: Value households · 2+ adults · price-led last 3 buys
bounds: price led the last three coffee buys
cohorts.tension: wants a treat / shares the pack

cohorts.label: Cafe switcher
cohorts.rule: Cafe switchers · 1+ cafe coffee / week · tried canned
bounds: one or more cafe coffees a week

mains.text: Walk me through a weekday morning drink.
Who else is in that moment with you?
When you want cold coffee out of home, what comes to mind first?
What have you tried and dropped?
Here is Aroha. What is this for, in your week?
What would make you pay cafe money for a can?

probes.text: Keep going. That contradicts the price line.

documents.title: Bengaluru office weekday
documents.text: Weekday morning is Bru or instant at the flat, then a cab. Cold coffee out of home means a can for the cab to the client site, not a cafe stop. I do not have a brand I trust in a can. Cafe coffee looks like a treat. A can looks like I packed breakfast. I can drink it at the desk and nobody asks if I am on a diet. Filter at a relative's house is a different drink. I will not pay cafe money unless the can tastes like that cafe cup and still looks ordinary on the desk.

documents.title: Delhi desk and cab
documents.text: The morning drink is mine. My flatmate is asleep. Out of home, cold coffee is for the back seat before a meeting in Gurgaon. I tried a sweet can that tasted like a milkshake and dropped it after one week. What I want is coffee I can open without a performance. If the can is very pretty I feel I have to explain it. Desk-safe means quiet, not a cafe cup with foam.

documents.title: Hyderabad campus canteen
documents.text: At the office canteen I still look for filter or Bru before I look for a can. Cold coffee from the machine is watery. A can is what I carry between buildings. I dropped a vanilla can because it did not taste like coffee. I would pay more only if the first sip is bitter enough to count as coffee and the can does not look like a protein drink.

documents.title: Pune two-adult household
documents.text: Two adults, one jar of coffee, and a fight about who finished it. A treat is allowed on Sunday. A can for one person feels selfish unless it is on offer. The last three buys were the cheaper jar, then a multipack, then whatever was on the Blinkit discount. I want the taste of a cafe once in a while and I also have to share the house budget. Do not make it a single fancy can I cannot justify.

documents.title: Kolkata shared pack
documents.text: My mother notices what comes into the fridge. A can I drink alone gets a comment. A multipack we both use does not. We dropped a sweet imported can because the price was a cafe price and the taste was sugar. Cold coffee out of home, for me, is still a roadside glass or Bru at the shop, not a brand can. If it is a treat, it has to be obviously shared.

documents.title: Mumbai cafe week
documents.text: I drink cafe coffee at least twice a week. The can is what I try when I am late, and then I resent it. Canned coffee is not my coffee. It smells sweet before it smells like coffee. I have tried three cans. I remember the one that tasted burnt and the one that tasted like chocolate milk. Convenience is real. Identity is also real. I do not want the can to pretend it is the cafe.

documents.title: Bengaluru third-cup comparison
documents.text: Filter at home, cafe near the office, can only in the airport. The airport can was cold and fine and forgettable. What I would pay cafe money for is a can that keeps the bitterness and skips the dessert flavour. I will not switch my cafe habit for a can that tastes like a shake. The trial was enough to know the category is not there yet.

documents.title: Blinkit RTD coffee review
documents.text: Tastes like medicine. I wanted cold coffee and got a protein shake. Will not buy again. The sweetness sits on top of a chalky note. This is not a desk drink and it is not a cafe drink.

documents.title: Amazon can as breakfast
documents.text: I keep this in the office bag. It looks like I packed breakfast, which is what I want. Taste is thin. Better than the medicinal one. Still would not serve it to someone who just came from a cafe.

documents.title: Price against a cafe cup
documents.text: Ninety rupees for a can and one hundred forty for the cafe downstairs. The can loses. I will pay cafe money only when the can tastes like coffee rather than flavoured milk. Until then I buy the offer price or I skip.

documents.title: Multipack for the house
documents.text: Bought the four-pack because both of us drink it. A single can feels like a personal luxury and I hear about it. Taste is acceptable if it is cold. Dropped the glass bottle because it was twice the money for the same sweet coffee.

documents.title: Kirana Bru versus can
documents.text: If I am near a kirana I ask for Bru or a coffee glass. The can is for when I cannot stop. Familiar taste beats a new brand I do not trust. Cold coffee from the fridge at home still starts with the jar we already know.

documents.title: Too sweet chemical finish
documents.text: First sip is sugar, finish is chemical. I wanted cold coffee, not dessert. Dropped after two cans. A cafe cup is bitter and short. This was long and sweet.

documents.title: Nescafe RTD comparison
documents.text: Nescafé RTD is the can I recognise. It is not loved. It is known. I trust known more than a new name. It still tastes sweeter than filter. I drink it in the cab and I do not talk about it.

documents.title: Not my coffee
documents.text: Tried it once between meetings. Canned coffee is not my coffee. Smell was confectionery. I went back to the cafe the same day. Convenience did not cover the loss of taste.

documents.title: Office sipper incidence
documents.text: Metro office drinkers age 25 to 34 who bought ready-to-drink coffee in the last 90 days. Tea-only respondents are a hard out. Member count in this gold slice is 12410. Incidence is higher in Bengaluru, Delhi, and Hyderabad than in smaller cities.

documents.title: Value household incidence
documents.text: Households with two or more adults whose last three coffee buys were price-led. Tea-only is a hard out. Member count in this gold slice is 8104. Shared packs outnumber single cans in this set.

documents.title: Cafe switcher incidence
documents.text: People who drink cafe coffee at least once a week and have tried a canned coffee. Tea-only is a hard out. Member count in this gold slice is 3276. The base is smaller than the office and value sets.

documents.title: Tea-only hard out
documents.text: Respondents who do not drink coffee are out of scope. Do not interview them as coffee buyers. A question that is only about tea, with no coffee, is outside the screener.
